newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan economy recovering, private demand firm--EPA.
newsitem.headline: Japan economy recovering, private demand firm--EPA.

text.p: Japan's economy is continuing to recover gradually and private demand is firm, the Economic Planning Agency (EPA) said in its monthly report on Friday.

It said although there were some effects from the rise in the sales tax on April 1 to five percent from three percent, consumption was gradually recovering and housing construction levels were still high.
The report also said that even though manufacturers were rather cautious about current business conditions, improvements were continuing. Non-manufacturers were cautious.
Industrial production was on a rising trend, helped by low inventory levels, an EPA official told reporters.

"Industry output is quite strong, inexplicably strong, even," he said, adding that the Trade Ministry's survey of manufacturers' forecasts of output for April and May predicted month-on-month rises of 1.9 percent and 1.1 percent respectively.
Exports were rather strong and imports were generally strong, the official said, adding that he expected exports to continue to rise and imports to be weak after April.
On consumption, he said department store sales were likely to fall by double digits in April from a year earlier but the reaction to the tax increase should fade by the end of June.
Supermarket sales were likely to recover a little earlier than department store sales and car sales were likely to fall in April and May, he said.
He added that income and employment indicators were doing "reasonably".
